hook: The naturalist whose voyage on the Beagle led him to the theory of evolution.

pages.x: Charles Darwin was born in 1809 in Shrewsbury, England, the son of a rich doctor. He was sent to study medicine in Edinburgh, but could not bear watching operations without anaesthetic. So his father sent him to Cambridge to become a clergyman.

At Cambridge he was mad about collecting beetles. Once, holding a rare beetle in each hand, he saw a third, and popped one into his mouth to free a hand. It squirted burning acid on his tongue, and he lost two of the three.

In 1831, aged 22, he joined the survey ship HMS Beagle as its naturalist, for a voyage around the world that lasted five years. He was seasick much of the time, but collected thousands of plants, animals and fossils.

In 1835 the Beagle reached the Galápagos Islands. Darwin rode the giant tortoises, and heard that you could tell which island a tortoise came from by its shell. Back home, the finches he brought turned out to be different species on different islands.
He worked out that living things vary, and those best suited to their surroundings survive and have more young. Over vast stretches of time, these small changes add up to new species.
pages.fx: It explained the variety of life without miracles, and became the foundation of all modern biology.

pages.x: Before proposing to his cousin Emma Wedgwood, he wrote a list. "Marry": children, a constant companion, "better than a dog anyhow". "Not marry": freedom, and more money for books. Marry won, and they had ten children.

At Down House in Kent he worked quietly for 20 years on his theory, afraid of the uproar it would cause. In 1858 a letter came from Alfred Russel Wallace, in the islands of Southeast Asia, with the very same idea.

He rushed out his book in 1859, and every copy was snapped up by booksellers on the first day. At a famous debate in Oxford, a bishop asked Darwin's friend Thomas Huxley whether it was on his grandfather's or his grandmother's side that he was descended from an ape.
His last book was about earthworms, and sold very well. He died in 1882 and was buried in Westminster Abbey, near Isaac Newton.
Darwin's theory of evolution is the foundation of modern biology: it explains how all living things, humans included, are related, and how they came to be.

Showed that all living things share common ancestors
